defects.claim:
The unit's URL route relies on the mapping's bare-string 400 arm to keep the <2-products exit byte-identical. On the current rebase target that arm no longer exists: W4-9 merged a codeless allowlist ({'Comparison failed', PRODUCT_PARSE_FAILURE_MESSAGE}), and anything else is redacted to 400 {code: INTERNAL_ERROR, error: INTERNAL_ERROR_FRIENDLY_MESSAGE}. 'Could not extract both products' is not on the list.

Reproduced by simulating the rebase: I extracted origin/main (cb1c64cb) app/ + tests/ with git archive into scratchpad rmeter_adv3/rb (no .env) and applied `git diff 1c6f6796 -- app tests` from this worktree.

defects.why_it_matters:
The brief says the orchestrator rebases after SOUND and believes origin/main is d70dd876, which lacks the W4-9 floor. Main has moved to cb1c64cb.

Once merged, an UNFLAGGED path forks for every caller: a URL extraction failure changes from 400 BAD_REQUEST 'Could not extract both products' to 400 INTERNAL_ERROR 'Something went wrong on our side'. That breaks the hard rule that unflagged changes stay byte-identical on every other path. It also makes the PR text's claim false ('The <2-products exit takes the mapping's bare-string 400 arm and gets the same body as before (pinned)').

The pins go red, so this cannot ship silently. But the fix then lands in the rebase step without adversarial review, and the easy 'fix' of re-pinning to the new body would accept the regression.

The ruling already asked this unit to compose with W4-9 (for the service check). The route arm does not.

Two fix options:
(a) At base, route only CODED results through the mapping and keep the blanket 400 for the code-less result. This is byte-identical at base and survives the rebase.
(b) Add 'Could not extract both products' to W4-9's allowlist at rebase time. This must be an explicit, reviewed decision.

The code itself is correct. Real-generate probes (a fake OpenAI client driving the real generate_comparison) give identical base and head records for error null, '', false, 0, [], {'error': null} and {}, via both the service and the route, with metering off and on.
